system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: a query that determines which sub-streams form the context for the operator
system_prompt_style.note: Context per LLM call is assembled from queried substreams of the output stream; no separate system prompt mechanism described. Paper only.

env_context_strategy.note: Not a repository/SWE harness; the paper does not describe any environment-context mechanism, and no config schema or code was available.

context_compaction.note: Substream query selects rows of the history for context ("selecting relevant rows based on specified conditions"), which does not map cleanly to any listed value. No code was available to confirm compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: consisting of text rows representing assignment formulas derived from operator executions

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: When generating new content, the LLM is tasked with producing the next line in the relevant substream, following the established format.
tool_call_format.note: The LLM emits an assignment row (Python-like formula) that is evaluated by SimpleEval. This is the closest value; there are no tool calls.

tool_count.note: No tool registry is described; the paradigm uses operators, not tools. Code was not in the evidence.

edit_primitive.note: No file-editing surface is described. Paper only.

protocol_standardization.note: No source code or dependency list was available to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The simulation progresses by evaluating operators sequentially, with each step potentially influencing which operator is executed next.
loop_primitives.note: Operator list with next-pointers acts as a programmable loop. In the social simulation example, inconsistent responses get one revision opportunity; that behaviour is specific to the example.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: a high-level strategic plan subject to selective revision, a detailed implementation plan
planning_granularity.note: Plans are state variables defined by user programs, not a harness plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Each character is controlled in its own stream
multi_agent_topology.note: A single program drives all entities; multi-entity simulations are expressed as substreams within it.

human_in_loop.note: The paper mentions humans could inquire, but no gating mechanism is described.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The simulation maintains a state composed of variables that can be modified at each step and influence the output.

self_verification.note: Format conformance resampling and program-defined consistency checks are mentioned but not described as a harness mechanism.

retry_policy.note: Step-level resampling on format error is mentioned ("reduced need for resampling"); that is not task-level retry.

termination_condition.note: The formal definition includes a set of termination conditions T, but the paper does not detail them.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote:
The expressions module provides a secure evalu-
ator for executing simulation expressions
execution_isolation.note: Formulas are evaluated in-process with SimpleEval. This is based on the paper description only.

tracing.evidence_quote:
This provides a trace-
able record of the LLM’s behavior and outputs
tracing.note: The output stream serves as a per-step record; a metrics file option also exists.

eval_hooks.note: RL benchmark tasks exist as configs per the paper; the repository was not available to confirm them.

guardrails.evidence_quote:
The expressions module provides a secure evalu-
ator for executing simulation expressions
guardrails.note: A restricted evaluator limits what executed formulas can do.

designed to efficiently control and leverage
Large Language Models (LLMs) for complex, dynamic simulations and agentic workflows

open_source.note: The repository is public per the paper footnote, but the LICENSE was not in the evidence.

model_agnostic.note: The default model is gemini-1.5-pro and only Gemini models were evaluated. The client abstraction was not visible in the evidence.
